auth.deleted.body: The live database, every site and every recorded pageview have been removed, and payment-provider deletion has completed. Storage and recovery systems outside the application follow their operators' retention controls and are not used to reactivate this account.
auth.deleted.title: Your account is gone
auth.error.bad_credentials: That email address and password do not match an account.
auth.error.code_cancelled: Too many wrong codes — that one has been cancelled. Ask for a new one.
auth.error.code_expired: That code has expired. Ask for a new one.
auth.error.confirm_code: That confirmation code is not right. Check the email, or send a new code.
auth.error.confirm_delete: Type the domain exactly to confirm the deletion.
auth.error.confirm_reset: Type the domain exactly to confirm the reset.
auth.error.domain_taken: That domain is already being tracked. If it is yours and you have lost access, get in touch.
auth.error.domain_taken_elsewhere: That domain is already being tracked by another site.
auth.error.email_invalid: That does not look like an email address.
auth.error.email_taken: An account already uses that email address. Sign in instead, or reset your password.
auth.error.google_account: That account signs in with Google. Use the Google button above.
auth.error.google_exchange: We could not complete the Google sign-in. Start again from the sign-in page.
auth.error.google_no_code: Google did not return a sign-in code. Start again from the sign-in page.
auth.error.google_state: The sign-in could not be verified. Start again from the sign-in page.
auth.error.internal: Something went wrong on our side. Try again, and tell us if it keeps happening.
auth.error.no_code: There is no code outstanding. Ask for a new one.
auth.error.reset_expired: That reset link has expired. Ask for a new one.
auth.error.reset_invalid: That reset link is not valid. Ask for a new one.
auth.error.reset_used: That reset link has already been used. Ask for a new one.
auth.error.too_many_attempts: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
auth.error.too_many_logins: Too many sign-in attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again.
auth.error.too_many_registrations: Too many accounts created from here. Wait a few minutes and try again.
auth.error.totp_code: That code is not right. Check the time on your phone, then try the next code.
auth.error.two_factor_code: That code is not right. Check your authenticator app, or use a recovery code.
auth.error.two_factor_locked: Your team requires two-factor authentication, so it cannot be turned off.
auth.error.two_factor_required: Your team requires two-factor authentication. Set it up to carry on.
auth.error.type_delete: Type DELETE in the box to confirm.
auth.error.verify_link: That link has expired or has already been used. Sign in and ask for a new code.

auth.exports.help: A ZIP of the ten roll-up tables plus raw_events.csv — every event, one row each. The raw export is in every plan: data you generated on your own site is yours. A prepared archive can be downloaded for 24 hours and is then deleted.
auth.exports.title: Export everything
auth.flash.account_deleted: Your account, its database and every site in it have been deleted.
auth.flash.code_sent: We sent a new code to {email}.
auth.flash.confirm_sent: We sent a code to your email address. It expires in ten minutes.
auth.flash.device_revoked: That device has been signed out.
auth.flash.domain_changed_one: The domain has been changed. The old one keeps collecting for the next {count} hour, so update your snippet before then.
auth.flash.domain_changed_other: The domain has been changed. The old one keeps collecting for the next {count} hours, so update your snippet before then.
auth.flash.email_confirmed: Your email is confirmed. Add your first site to start collecting.

auth.flash.recovery_regenerated: Your old recovery codes no longer work.
auth.flash.reset_sent: If an account uses {email}, a reset link is on its way. It expires in an hour.
auth.flash.stats_reset: Every recorded pageview for this site has been deleted. Your goals and settings are untouched.
auth.flash.team_saved: Your team settings have been saved.
auth.forgot.subtitle: Tell us your email address and we will send a link that works once.
auth.forgot.title: Reset your password
auth.google.help: One authorisation per site. Connecting a second site with the same Google account creates a second, independent grant — revoking one can never disconnect the other.
auth.google.title: Analytics history and search performance
auth.imports.client_error_size: That file is larger than 200 MB. Export a smaller date range and try again.
auth.imports.client_error_type: Choose the ZIP from Plausible, or a supported CSV file.
auth.imports.csv_help: One CSV, or a ZIP of them. A column we do not recognise stops the import and names the column, rather than being dropped quietly into numbers that are too small. The formats understood are:
auth.imports.dimensions_help: Pages, sources, countries, devices and the other dimensions included in your export.
auth.imports.drop_help: or click to choose it · ZIP up to 200 MB
auth.imports.error_choose_file: Choose a CSV or a ZIP to import.
auth.imports.error_google_incomplete: Google would not complete that authorisation — try connecting again.
auth.imports.error_unreadable_upload: That upload could not be read.
auth.imports.flash_connected: Connected. This grant belongs to this site alone.
auth.imports.flash_deleted: Import deleted, along with the history it brought in.
auth.imports.flash_disconnected: Disconnected. Other sites connected to the same Google account are untouched.
auth.imports.flash_export_started: Preparing your export. The download appears below and stays available for 24 hours.
auth.imports.history_help: Your past traffic stays visible alongside every new visit Feasible collects.
auth.imports.list_empty: Nothing has been imported into this site yet.
auth.imports.list_empty_help: Your first migration will appear here with live progress.
auth.imports.list_help: Follow every migration from upload to completion.
auth.imports.plausible_lede: Bring your complete analytics history with you. Upload the export exactly as Plausible gives it to you—we unpack every CSV, map the data, and keep you informed all the way through.
auth.imports.privacy_note: Processed privately for this site. Your archive is never shared.
auth.imports.safe_help: We validate before writing. If something is wrong, the import stops and tells you exactly what needs attention.
auth.imports.search_console_delay: Search Console data reaches Google about 24 to 36 hours late, so today and usually yesterday are empty here. That is Google's delay, not a gap in your tracking.
auth.imports.step_export_help: Download the ZIP from your site settings.
auth.imports.step_review_help: See progress, then explore the imported data.
auth.imports.step_upload_help: No unzipping, renaming or cleanup required.
auth.imports.upload_help: Choose the ZIP you downloaded from Plausible. We will recognise and import every supported CSV inside it.
auth.imports.upload_title: Upload one file. We handle the rest.
auth.layout.tagline: Privacy-first analytics. No cookies, no persistent identifiers.
auth.login.subtitle: Welcome back.
auth.login.title: Sign in
auth.onboarding.check_help: We will fetch {url} and tell you exactly what we found — the snippet, the wrong domain, or a policy blocking it.
auth.onboarding.received_body: Your first pageview has arrived. {site} is collecting.
auth.onboarding.title: Install {site}
auth.onboarding.verify_unreachable: We could not load the page
auth.onboarding.verify_wrong_domain: The snippet names a different site
auth.onboarding.waiting_help_one: Deploy the snippet and open your site in another tab. A brand-new domain can take up to {count} second to start collecting while our ingest tier picks it up, so a moment of nothing here is normal. This panel updates on its own — you do not need to reload.
auth.onboarding.waiting_help_other: Deploy the snippet and open your site in another tab. A brand-new domain can take up to {count} seconds to start collecting while our ingest tier picks it up, so a moment of nothing here is normal. This panel updates on its own — you do not need to reload.
auth.paths.error_unreadable_form: That form could not be read.
auth.paths.flash_saved_one: Saved. {count} stored path now reports under a cleaned route, retroactively.
auth.paths.flash_saved_other: Saved. {count} stored paths now report under a cleaned route, retroactively.
auth.paths.flash_slash_off: Trailing slashes are no longer merged.
auth.paths.flash_slash_on: /about and /about/ now report as one page, including in the history you already have.
auth.paths.lede: Merge URLs that are really one page — an id in a path, a trailing slash — into the route you think in. Rules are applied at query time, so they fix the history you already have, and at ingest, so the path dimension stops growing. They are tried in order and the first match wins.
auth.paths.legacy_notice: Upgrade note: older versions rewrote paths while a rule was active. Those lost originals cannot be reconstructed; removing a rule restores only originals retained by this version.
auth.paths.preview_empty: These rules would not merge anything on this site.
auth.paths.preview_help: This is exactly what saving these rules would do, and how many stored rows each merge moves. Nothing has been saved yet.
auth.paths.rules_help: A pattern is a regular expression. A replacement may refer back to a capture group with $1. For traffic stored by this version, deleting every rule puts retained original paths back.
auth.paths.trailing_slash_help: Most sites serve the same page at /about and /about/, and the two are otherwise two permanent rows on every report. A few sites genuinely serve different content at each, so this ships switched off rather than decided for you.
auth.reauth.help: We email a code because your account signs in with Google and has no password to ask for.
auth.recovery_codes.body: Each code works once. They are the only way into your account if you lose your phone — and this is the only time we can show them to you, because we store only their hashes.
auth.recovery_codes.title: Save your recovery codes
auth.recovery_codes.warning: Print them, or put them in your password manager. Not in the same place as your password.
auth.register.name: Name
auth.register.password_help: At least 12 characters. Length is the only rule — a passphrase is fine.
auth.register.subtitle: Every feature, one flat price, 30 days free. No card.
auth.register.title: Create your account
auth.reset.invalid: Reset links last an hour and can only be used once.
auth.reset.subtitle: Every device signed in to this account will be signed out.
auth.reset.title: Choose a new password
auth.settings_account.change_password_he: Every other signed-in browser is signed out when you change it.
auth.settings_account.delete_body: This immediately deletes your team, every site in it and the live database that holds all of your traffic, and requests deletion of your payment-provider customer with hourly retries after failure. Storage and recovery systems outside the application follow their operators' retention controls and are not used to reactivate the account.
auth.settings_account.delete_confirm: Delete your account and every site in it? This cannot be undone.
auth.settings_account.name: Name
auth.settings_account.set_password_help: You sign in with Google. Adding a password gives you a second way in.
auth.settings_security.disable_help: We ask for your password again, because a stolen session cookie must not be enough to remove the thing that protects you from a stolen session cookie.
auth.settings_security.enrol_heading: Scan this with your authenticator app
auth.settings_security.manual_key: Cannot scan? Type this key into your app instead:
auth.settings_security.off_help: You will need an authenticator app — 1Password, Authy, Google Authenticator, or anything else that does TOTP.
auth.settings_security.qr_alt: QR code for your authenticator app
auth.settings_security.recovery_help: Generating a new set immediately invalidates the old one.
auth.settings_security.recovery_low: Generate a new set before you run out.
auth.settings_security.subtitle: A six-digit code from your phone on top of your password. Your secret is encrypted before it touches disk.
auth.settings_sessions.subtitle: Every browser signed in to your account. A session ends by itself after 14 days without use.
auth.settings_team.grace: If a subscription lapses we keep accepting your traffic until {date}. Losing data you can never get back is not an acceptable consequence of a card expiring.
auth.settings_team.name: Team name
auth.settings_team.require_2fa_help: Anybody in this team who has not set it up lands on the enrolment screen on their next page load, rather than being locked out. Nobody in the team can turn their own off while this is on.
auth.shields.country_hint: Two-letter ISO country codes. Useful when a country is entirely bot traffic for your site.
auth.shields.empty: No rules of this kind yet.
auth.shields.error_aggregate_hostname: The aggregate hostname bucket cannot be allowed. Add a specific hostname instead.
auth.shields.error_unreadable_form: That form could not be read.
auth.shields.flash_added: {rule} is now blocked. It takes effect on the next event.
auth.shields.flash_hostname_allowed: {hostname} is now allowed. New events take effect immediately.
auth.shields.hostname_hint: Additional allowed hostnames. The registered domain and its subdomains are always accepted; add preview or checkout hosts that live elsewhere.
auth.shields.ip_hint: Checked in the ingest tier, which is the only place the raw address exists. An address or a CIDR block.
auth.shields.lede: Traffic you do not want counted. Blocked addresses are checked in the ingest tier — the only place the raw IP still exists — and everything else is checked at the shard where these rules are live. A change here applies within about fifteen seconds.
auth.shields.not_public_address: This is not your public address.
auth.shields.own_traffic_help: This is the address this page resolved you to, using exactly the same header precedence the event endpoint uses. Blocking it here blocks the traffic you generate yourself.
auth.shields.page_hint: A path, or a path ending in * to block everything under it. Staging routes and health checks live here.
auth.shields.rejected_hint: These hostnames recently sent events for this site but were not allowed. Review each hostname before allowing future traffic.
auth.shields.warning_private: This is a private or shared proxy address, not the visitor's public one. Every visitor currently resolves to this address, so manually blocking it would block everyone. The one-click action is hidden until the proxy is fixed. Add the proxy to FEASIBLE_INGEST_TRUSTED_PROXIES and have it append X-Forwarded-For.
auth.shields.warning_unresolved: We could not work out your address from this request, so a rule built here would not match your traffic.
auth.site_new.display_name_help: What you want to see in the list. Useful when the domain is
auth.site_new.domain_help: Paste a full URL if that is easier — we will take the hostname out of it.
auth.site_new.subtitle: One snippet, and you are collecting.
auth.site_new.title: Add a site
auth.site_new.tz_help: This is what "today" means on every chart for this site.
auth.site_row.pin_title: Pin this site to the top
auth.site_settings.danger_help: These cannot be undone. Both ask you to type the domain first.
auth.site_settings.delete_confirm: Delete {domain} and all of its data? This cannot be undone.
auth.site_settings.details_help: What this site is called, when its days start, and who can see it.
auth.site_settings.domain_help_one: The old domain keeps collecting for {count} hour, so you can change it here first and update the snippet when you deploy. Nothing else moves: your history, goals and settings belong to the site, not to its name.
auth.site_settings.domain_help_other: The old domain keeps collecting for {count} hours, so you can change it here first and update the snippet when you deploy. Nothing else moves: your history, goals and settings belong to the site, not to its name.
auth.site_settings.dual_write_body: {domain} keeps working for another {duration}, so a snippet you have not updated yet is not losing data. Your goals, funnels and history all moved with the site — they are keyed on the site, never on the domain.
auth.site_settings.public_help: Anyone with the link sees this site's traffic, with no sign-in.
auth.site_settings.reset_body: Deletes every pageview and visit recorded for this site. Your goals, settings and the site itself are untouched.
auth.site_settings.reset_confirm: Delete every recorded pageview for {domain}? This cannot be undone.
auth.site_settings.snippet_help: Paste this into every page you want counted, just before </head>.
auth.site_settings.timezone_help: Changing this re-buckets every chart by the new local day.
auth.site_settings.traffic_warning: Traffic is still arriving for this domain — remember to remove the snippet from your site. Until you do, every visitor is loading a script for a site that no longer exists.
auth.site_settings.transfer_help: Move this site to another team you own or administer. Its history stays with the site; guests, pending invitations and shared links are revoked.
auth.sites.empty_body: Add the first one and we will give you a snippet, tell you where to paste it, and wait with you for the first pageview.
auth.sites.folder_delete_confirm: Delete this folder? The sites inside it move back to the top level.
auth.sites.locked_body: Analytics are hidden while this account is not currently paying. Your sites, settings, and collected data remain here.
auth.sites.title: Sites
auth.title.google_disabled: Google sign-in is not set up
auth.two_factor.recovery_help: Lost your phone? Type one of your recovery codes here instead.
auth.two_factor.subtitle: Open your authenticator app and enter the current code.
auth.two_factor.title: Two-factor code
auth.verify.link_too: The email also has a link that signs you straight in.
auth.verify.title: Confirm your email
